infrastructure: Lima data centre market growing; Claro and Movistar Peru deploying 5G in major cities
Significant infrastructure gap between Lima and rural/Andean regions
Dorsal Nacional de Fibra Óptica project extending connectivity to underserved areas
talent: Pontificia Universidad Católica del Perú and UTEC producing engineering graduates with improving AI focus
Growing Lima tech community with Platzi and Crehana driving digital skills development
Brain drain to Chile, Spain, and the US significant among top technical talent
governance: Personal data protection law (Ley 29733) providing baseline governance framework
National AI Strategy 2026-2030 (ENIA) approved via Resolución Ministerial N° 152-2026-PCM, effective May 2, 2026, binding for the public sector
Political instability (multiple presidents in recent years) disrupts policy continuity
investment: Smaller VC ecosystem than Colombia or Chile; Kushki and Culqi as notable fintech AI examples
Mining sector AI investment growing as international companies seek efficiency in copper and gold operations
Start-Up Peru government programme funding early-stage tech companies
economic_readiness: 33M population with growing urban middle class; Lima represents a concentrated AI adoption market
Mining and agriculture sectors creating AI demand for extraction optimisation and precision farming
Significant informal economy (70%+ of employment) limiting structured AI deployment in many sectors
